summary: An excellent, comprehensive mission design for ZYZZsat. All required elements are addressed with verified hand calculations, STK evidence (Images 1-5, Appendix A), well-justified trade-offs, and honest acknowledgement of limitations. To reach the very top of the Accomplished band, strengthen the link budget, eclipse/beta-angle treatment, decay sensitivity, and GSD analysis, and consider discussing alternative mission concepts in Section 1.
next_steps: Add an X-band link budget to Section 2.4 (margin, antenna gains, achievable data rates) to complement the data-volume budget in Table 6, closing the gap you honestly flagged.
In Section 2.1/Table 1, present eclipse duration as a function of beta angle over the year rather than a fixed ~34 min per orbit, e.g. a plot of eclipse time versus beta angle from STK.

Extend the Section 2.5 decay analysis with a sensitivity study (varying density/scale height or running multiple STK cases) to bound the re-entry date, and analyse detector IFOV/sampling and pointing jitter effects on the 5 m GSD in Section 2.3.
In Section 2.2, quantify the rideshare orbit compatibility risk for Vega C (altitude/injection tolerances) and state explicit acceptance criteria for the fallback option.

In Section 1, briefly discuss alternative mission concepts (e.g. constellation vs single spacecraft, alternative payloads) and why they were rejected; also improve figure resolution and add page numbers to the table of contents.

criteria.C1: Accomplished (9/10). Section 1 addresses all requirements: primary mission (5 m GSD imaging of the Great Barrier Reef), need (bleaching statistics, gaps in existing products), single-spacecraft justification, and users (AIMS as operator, multiple customers), all well referenced [1]-[6]. To reach full marks, add a brief discussion of alternative mission concepts considered and why the single-spacecraft approach was preferred over, say, a small constellation.
criteria.C2: Accomplished (54/60). Section 2 is comprehensive: launch trade table with azimuth calculation (2.2), hand-derived orbit elements verified in STK including i = 97.79° (2.3, Table 4), explicit manoeuvres, ground station access analysis with six daily passes (2.4, Table 5), data budget, and a five-year mission with drag-sail EOL and decay calculations (2.5). Screenshots, tables, references and Appendix A files are all present. Full marks require closing the missing X-band link budget, treating eclipse duration as beta-angle dependent, bounding the decay estimate, and analysing GSD beyond the diffraction/pixel-count argument.
criteria.C3: Accomplished (9/10). Section 3 reaches specific, quantitative conclusions (revisit times, pass rates, decay lifetime) and honestly identifies four limitations with proposed next steps, showing genuine design insight. To reach full marks, tie each limitation to a concrete, prioritised action with expected impact on the design (e.g. which analysis would most change the orbit or EOL choice).
criteria.C4: Accomplished (18/20). The report has a clear structure with executive summary, numbered sections, consistently labelled figures and tables, matched citations [1]-[15] in IEEE style, and concise professional writing. Minor deductions relate to some low-resolution figures and a table of contents without page numbers; ensure all figures are high-resolution and formatting is fully consistent throughout.
